doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

chapter: Florida bands and New Orleans comparison
title: Early Florida piano players and ragtime
summary: Billie names women pianists Willie Woods and Florida Beck, party-playing before bands, Josie in New Orleans, and Florida trumpeter Joe Jesse.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I'm wondering if you remember any of the early piano players over in Florida. Can you remember either men or women, aside from your own family? Who they were, how they played, what style of...
Oh, they played this old... Everyone that played was all my style of playing. It's like I play now. All jazz.

Yeah, plenty ragtime music. There was a girl named Willie Woods. Willie Woods. She was a great piano player. There was Florida Beck. She was a number one piano player. Was a woman? Yeah. Two women of course.
Both of them, they... Yeah. So, Miss Woods was a...
Yeah, Woods was a piano... And also Miss Beck.
And also... Well, where did they work, those women?
Where would they work? In a band or did they work in the bar rooms?

They worked in different bands. Well, I mean, you know bands, but they ain't like theirs now, you see. Yeah, I understand. But they scattered around, you see. But most of them, most of them parties, see. People in the other days used to just have a party and hire piano players to play, you know, like that. Before the band thing got out, you know, like there, see. Then there's a girl right here now. I met Far Taken Sick. ! She named Josie. Josie. Yeah, Josie. She's living over the river. She's a little slender, bronze, can't go. She flipped some piano. Really? I see her use a team together, right. See?
I'd like to hear her. She's still here, isn't she?
Yeah, I met her. She was here. She lived over the river somewhere. She did tell me, but she told me that when she come over again that she was coming to see me.
Well, she still played piano, do you think?
She told me she, she told me she ain't playing no more.

She quit. Yeah, she's playing in bands. She's playing in different bands like I was, see. And then, let's see. Nice band. Then another fella, he's there now, Joe Jesse. He was a trumpet player. He's from out of my hometown out of Florida. Yes. He was a great trumpet player. And also, a drummer called Teddy Bear in my hometown. Teddy Bear. He's, oh, he's there now, I guess. I'm not sure he's there now. There was, uh, the Douglas, Douglas, uh, Butts of Douglas. They had an orchestra. Big band. That's in Florida, Pensacola.
